solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sun's somehow keeping house policy's irreverence

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one group of letters wraps round the other
done somehow means done in some unstated way, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: the letters of the word, the apostrophe dropped
HO is the standard abbreviation for house
a party line is a policy; the 's is read as 'is', joining to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a newspaper's attitude to the royal house is disrespectful.
explanation.walkthrough: SUNS rearranged as UN...SS holds HO and LINE, giving UNHOLINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Unholiness is a lack of piety or reverence, a near synonym of irreverence.

clue.text: Savoury taste of cumin, nothing extreme, captivating mother

indicators.note: to captivate is figuratively to hold captive, so the middle letters enclose another piece
with no extreme left, the first and last letters are cut off and only the inner part stays

parts.note: the inner letters of the spice name
MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A cook describes the savoury flavour of cumin, not overpowering, that delights their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of cumin' looks like part of the definition, but 'of' only links and cumin is the source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the Japanese name for the fifth basic taste, the meaty savoury flavour.

clue.text: Cutting tool husband used on border with more spruce

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
an edge is a border
spruce means neat, so more spruce is trimmer

explanation.surface: A husband takes a cutting tool to the garden border to make it neater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' tempts as the tree being cut, but here it is the adjective meaning neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge trimmer is a powered or hand tool with blades for cutting hedges.

clue.text: Regularly flaunt variable jump on ice

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
in algebra x, y and z stand for variables

explanation.surface: A skater keeps showing off a changeable leap on the rink.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutz is a figure-skating jump taken off from the back outside edge of one skate.

clue.text: Tended feverish user in middle of London

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
only the central letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the six-letter city name

indicators.note: feverish activity is agitated and jumbled, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: Someone looked after a feverish patient in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feverish' and 'Tended' together suggest nursing a sick person, but feverish is only stirring the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to care for them, so nursed is the past tense synonym of tended.

clue.text: Cross after minor operation brought about complaint

indicators.note: the cross is placed after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: minor means small

indicators.note: brought about is turned round, as a ship goes about, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: OP is the short form of operation
a cross is written as X

explanation.surface: A patient got angry after a small operation led to an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for an angry patient but is the letter X. Complaint is used in its medical sense, an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness or disease, and smallpox is a contagious viral disease.

clue.text: A Parisian, on time, briefly meets Edward without interruption

indicators.note: made brief, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: UN is the French for a
punctual means on time
Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, arriving on time, has a short meeting with Edward that nobody breaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctuation marks break up text, so writing that is unpunctuated runs on with no breaks or pauses.

clue.text: Ballad penned by each musician

indicators.note: something penned by another is shut inside it, as in a pen

parts.note: per means each, as in 'a pound per head'
a lay is a narrative song or ballad

explanation.surface: A song written by every member of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests songwriting, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is one who plays an instrument, so any musician is a player.

clue.text: German car with corrosion knocked back inspector

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word runs right to left

parts.note: rot is decay or corrosion

explanation.surface: A German car eaten by rust is turned down by a vehicle inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects accounts officially, so the word is a kind of inspector.

clue.text: Invalidate article Greek character left

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A legal clause demanding that a Greek figure's written piece be cancelled after he departed.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, which is to invalidate it.

clue.text: Horny creature, one primarily beguiling former partner

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A randy character charming an old flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' reads as lustful, but the creature simply has horns.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat with long curved horns, so it is literally horned.

clue.text: Jean curtailed rubbish, being green?

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the name taken as written
lousy means rubbish, very poor

explanation.surface: Jean, cut short, says the effort is useless because it is not eco-friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks environmental; the question mark flags the other sense, green with envy.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is called being green, from the idiom 'green-eyed monster' for jealousy.

clue.text: One who excavates square uncovered waterway lacking volume

indicators.note: with its covering stripped off, the word keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: the word with its outer letters removed

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a river is a natural waterway
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: A digger works on a square that has no roof and a canal running dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrier digs stone out of a quarry, so the word names a kind of excavator.

clue.text: Cry of surprise initially falling upon island

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letters of the following words are used

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in surprise as they land on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is everyday British slang, like 'wow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Place to gamble on savings account, Charlie having retired

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the whole string of letters runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an ISA is a British tax-free savings account
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A pensioner gambles away their savings once Charlie has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: ISA stands for Individual Savings Account, a UK tax-free product. ON, ISA and C read together backwards make CASINO.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where gambling games are played.

clue.text: Award huge coach

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, used in clothing sizes
a coach is a railway carriage, also called a car

explanation.surface: A prize of a giant bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a trainer or bus; here it is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the popular name for the Academy Award statuette given for film.

clue.text: Item of data on popular type of drug

parts.note: a stat is a single statistic
in means popular, fashionable; 'on' places it after the first piece

explanation.surface: A statistic on a widely prescribed kind of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Statins are a class of drugs prescribed to lower cholesterol.

clue.text: Swiss resort represented most ostentatious luxury

indicators.note: re-presented in another form, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
the Ritz hotel stands for showy luxury, as in 'ritzy'

explanation.surface: A Swiss ski resort stands for the showiest kind of opulence.
explanation.definitionFit: St Moritz is a famous upmarket ski resort in the Engadine valley of Switzerland.

clue.text: With Ecstasy gone, supply crack

indicators.note: gone means departed, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to equip is to supply with what is needed
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: With one drug unavailable, the dealer supplies crack cocaine instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like the drug, but it is a crack in the sense of a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, and a quip is a short clever joke.

clue.text: Fraudster prosecuted reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard spoken, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: sued means taken to court; the p is silent

explanation.surface: A conman was reportedly taken to court.
explanation.walkthrough: The P is silent, as in psychology.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud is a pretentious person, a fake who claims knowledge they lack, so a kind of fraud.

clue.text: Top half of planet seen by Jack somewhere in the Hebrides

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is kept, the rest being dropped

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
Uranus is the seventh planet

explanation.surface: From up north, Jack spots the upper part of a planet over a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'top half' is the first three letters of URANUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jura is an island in the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Fiona evidently conceals birthmarks

indicators.note: to conceal is to keep something out of sight inside, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: spanning the end of the name and start of the adverb

explanation.surface: Fiona is plainly covering up some marks on her skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi is the plural of naevus, the medical term for a birthmark or mole.

clue.text: Keeper right to return American casual shirt

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: RT is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
US is short for American
a tee is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper has the right to go back to wearing an American leisure top.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee holds and looks after property on behalf of others, so is a keeper of it.

clue.text: Draconian press worker joins media chief

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
ED is short for editor, the head of a paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper employee teams up with a harsh boss in the media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspaper trade, which 'media chief' reinforces, but it is the verb iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means extremely harsh, and ironhanded means ruling with severe, unyielding strictness.
